summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for left upper quadrant abdominal pain near her gastrostomy tube site. She has a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and cyclic vomiting syndrome requiring a gastrostomy tube for nutritional support. She underwent fluoroscopy-guided replacement of the gastrostomy tube due to malposition and granulation tissue at the site, which was treated with silver nitrate. Post-procedure, her pain improved, and she tolerated oral intake. The decision was made not to restart tube feeds due to anatomical concerns. She was restarted on home medications with an increase in nortriptyline to 100 mg nightly for pain management and discharged home with instructions for tube site care, pain control, and follow-up endoscopy.
